title.zh: 卷一百六十一 列傳第八十六 張趙李鄭徐王馮庾
title.en: Volume 161 Biographies 86: Zhang, Zhao, Li, Zheng, Xu, Wang, Feng, Yu
title.raw: 卷一百六十一 列傳第八十六 張趙李鄭徐王馮庾 Volume 161 Biographies 86: Zhang, Zhao, Li, Zheng, Xu, Wang, Feng, Yu

sentences.zh: 張趙李鄭徐王馮庾

translations.literal: Zhang, Zhao, Li, Zheng, Xu, Wang, Feng, and Yu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, Zhao, Li, Zheng, Xu, Wang, Feng, and Yu

sentences.zh: 張薦，字孝舉，深州陸澤人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jian, style name Xiaoju, was a man of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian, whose courtesy name was Xiaoju, came from Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖鷟，字文成，早惠絕倫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhuo, style name Wencheng, was precocious beyond compare in youth.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhang Zhuo, courtesy name Wencheng, had been exceptionally gifted from childhood.

sentences.zh: 為兒時，夢紫文大鳥，五色成文，止其廷。

translations.literal: As a child he dreamed of a great bird with purple markings, its five colors forming patterns, alighting in his courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: In childhood he dreamed of a great bird marked in purple, its five colors woven into patterns, which came to rest in his courtyard.

sentences.zh: 大父曰：「吾聞五色赤文，鳳也；

translations.literal: His great-grandfather said: "I have heard that five colors with red markings is the phoenix;"
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather said, "I have heard that when the five colors show red markings, the bird is a phoenix;"

sentences.zh: 紫文，鸑鷟也。

translations.literal: purple markings is the zhuoyu."
translations.idiomatic: when they show purple markings, it is a zhuoyu."

sentences.zh: 若壯，殆以文章瑞朝廷乎？

translations.literal: When you reach manhood, will you perhaps bring literary glory to the court as an auspice?"
translations.idiomatic: When you grow up, will you perhaps bring the court a literary omen?"

sentences.zh: 」遂命以名。

translations.literal: " He then gave him that name.
translations.idiomatic: With that he gave him his name.

sentences.zh: 調露初，登進士第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tiaolu era he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tiaolu reign he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 考功員外郎騫味道見所對，稱天下無雙。

translations.literal: Examination-section vice director Qian Weidao, seeing his answers, declared him unmatched under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Weidao of the Ministry of Rites, reading his examination papers, declared him unmatched anywhere under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 授岐王府參軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed aide in the Prince of Qi's household.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed an aide in the household of the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 八以制舉皆甲科，再調長安尉，遷鴻臚丞。

translations.literal: Eight times in the decree examinations he took first rank; twice transferred as Chang'an county lieutenant, then promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He took top honors in the decree examinations eight times, served twice as lieutenant of Chang'an County, and was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 四參選，判策為銓府最。

translations.literal: In four selection rounds his policy essay ranked highest in the Board of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In four rounds of civil selection his policy essay ranked first in the Board of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 員外郎員半千數為公卿稱「鷟文辭猶青銅錢，萬選萬中」，時號鷟「青錢學士」。

translations.literal: Vice director Yuan Banqian repeatedly told the high ministers that "Zhuo's literary compositions are like bronze coins—ten thousand selections, ten thousand hits," and the age styled Zhuo the "Bronze-Coin Academician."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yuan Banqian often told the chief ministers that Zhang Zhuo's prose was like bronze cash—pick ten thousand times and hit every time—and contemporaries called him the Bronze-Coin Academician.

sentences.zh: 證聖中，天官侍郎劉奇以鷟及司馬锽為御史。

translations.literal: In the Zhengsheng era, Vice Director of the Bureau of Astronomy Liu Qi nominated Zhuo and Sima Zheng as censors.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengsheng period, Vice Director Liu Qi of the Bureau of Astronomy recommended Zhuo and Sima Zheng for posts as censors.

sentences.zh: 性躁卞，儻蕩無檢，罕為正人所遇，姚崇尤惡之。

translations.literal: By nature he was irascible and unrestrained, rarely meeting with approval from upright men; Yao Chong especially detested him.
translations.idiomatic: He was irascible by nature and heedless in conduct, seldom winning favor from upright officials; Yao Chong detested him above all.

sentences.zh: 開元初，御史李全交劾鷟多口語訕短時政，貶嶺南；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, Censor Li Quanjiao impeached Zhuo for much loose talk mocking current policy, and he was demoted to Lingnan;
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan reign, Censor Li Quanjiao impeached Zhuo for loose talk that mocked current policy, and he was banished to Lingnan;

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書李日知訟斥太重，得內徙。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Li Rizhi argued that the penalty was too severe, and he was allowed an internal transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Li Rizhi protested that the punishment was too harsh, and Zhuo was allowed to move to a nearer post within the empire.

sentences.zh: 鷟屬文下筆輒成，浮艷少理致，其論著率詆誚蕪猥，然大行一時，晚進莫不傳記。

translations.literal: Zhuo's compositions flowed from his brush at once; they were florid and slight in reason, and his treatises mostly derided things as coarse and base, yet they flourished for a time and younger men all copied and transmitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhuo wrote at a stroke whatever he took up; his work was ornate and thin on substance, and his essays mostly sneered at others as vulgar—yet for a season they dominated fashion, and younger writers copied and circulated them without fail.

sentences.zh: 武後時，中人馬仙童陷默啜，問：「文成在否？

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time, the eunuch Ma Xiantong, captured by Mohechuo, was asked: "Is Wencheng still alive?"
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, the palace eunuch Ma Xiantong, taken prisoner by the Khitan ruler Mohechuo, was asked whether Wencheng was still alive.

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「近自御史貶官。

translations.literal: " He answered: "Recently demoted from censor."
translations.idiomatic: He answered that Zhuo had lately been demoted from the censorate.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「國有此人不用，無能為也。

translations.literal: " He said: "A state that has such a man and does not use him can accomplish nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Mohechuo said, "A state that possesses such a man and will not employ him can hope to accomplish nothing."

sentences.zh: 」新羅、日本使至，必出金寶購其文。

translations.literal: " Envoys from Silla and Japan, when they arrived, always brought gold and jewels to purchase his writings.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from Silla and Japan, whenever they arrived, would pay out gold and jewels to buy his writings.

sentences.zh: 終司門員外郎。

translations.literal: He ended as vice director of the Department of State Affairs' gate office.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as vice director of the gate office in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 薦敏銳有文辭，能為《周官》、《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: Jian was keen and possessed literary talent; he could expound the Rites of Zhou and the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian was quick-witted and skilled in letters; he could lecture on the Rites of Zhou and the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 初，為顏真卿嘆賞。

translations.literal: At first he won Yan Zhenqing's admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Early on he won the admiration of Yan Zhenqing.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，浙西觀察使李涵表薦才任史官，詔授左司禦率府兵曹參軍，以母老辭不就。

translations.literal: In the Dali era, Zhexi observation commissioner Li Han memorialized that Jian's talent suited him for the historiographer's office; an edict appointed him military aide in the Left Bureau of the Imperial Guard, but he declined on account of his mother's age.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali reign, Observation Commissioner Li Han of western Zhejiang memorialized that Jian's talent fitted him for the historiographer's office; the throne appointed him military aide in the Left Bureau of the Imperial Guard, but he declined because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 喪除，禮部侍郎於邵以聞，召充史館修撰，兼陽翟尉。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, Vice Minister of Rites Yu Shao reported this, and Jian was summoned to serve as compiler in the Historiography Institute, concurrently as magistrate of Yangzhai.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning ended, Vice Minister of Rites Yu Shao reported the matter, and Jian was summoned to the Historiography Institute as a compiler, while also serving as magistrate of Yangzhai.

sentences.zh: 真卿為李希烈所拘，遣兄子峴及家仆奏事，五輩皆留內客省，不得出。

translations.literal: Zhenqing, held by Li Xilie, sent his elder brother's son Xian and household servants to report affairs; all five parties were detained in the Inner Reception Office and could not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing, held prisoner by Li Xilie, sent his nephew Xian and household servants to present memorials at court; all five parties were detained in the Inner Reception Office and could not leave.

sentences.zh: 薦上疏曰：

translations.literal: Jian submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 去正月中，真卿奉使淮西，期不先戒，行無素備。

translations.literal: Last first month Zhenqing was sent on mission to Huaixi without prior warning of the date, and set out without customary preparations.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month just past, Yan Zhenqing was dispatched to Huaixi on imperial business without advance notice of the date and set out without the usual preparations.

sentences.zh: 受命之後，不宿於家，親黨不遑告別，介副不及陳請，孱僮單騎，即日載馳。

translations.literal: After receiving the command he did not lodge at home; relatives had no time to take leave; aides and deputies could not present their requests; with a frail servant he rode alone and set out that very day.
translations.idiomatic: Once he received the order he did not spend a night at home; kin had no chance to bid farewell; aides and deputies could not lodge their petitions; with only a frail servant he rode out alone that very day.

sentences.zh: 冒奸鋒於臨汝，折元惡於許下，捐軀杖義，威詬群兇，遂令脅制者回慮，忠勇者肆情。

translations.literal: He braved the traitors' blades at Linru and broke the arch-villain at Xuzhou, giving his body to uphold righteousness and awing the crowd of villains with his authority, so that those under coercion reconsidered and the loyal and brave gave full vent to their feelings.
translations.idiomatic: He braved the rebels' blades at Linru and broke the chief villain at Xuzhou, risking his person for righteousness and cowing the rebel host with his moral force, until those held under duress thought again and the loyal and brave gave full rein to their zeal.

sentences.zh: 周曾奮發於外，韋清伺應於內，希烈蒼黃窘迫，奔固舊穴，蓋真卿義風所激也。

translations.literal: Zhou Zeng roused himself without, Wei Qing watched for chances within, and Xilie, pale and hard pressed, fled to his old lair—surely stirred by Zhenqing's righteous example.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zeng stirred himself on the outside, Wei Qing coordinated from within, and Xilie, harried and in disarray, fled back to his old stronghold—all stirred, it seems, by Yan Zhenqing's example of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 真卿逮事四朝，為國元老，忠直孝友，羽儀王室。

translations.literal: Zhenqing served four reigns, was a senior pillar of the state, upright, loyal, filial, and friendly—a model for the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing had served four reigns, was a senior pillar of the state, and was upright, loyal, filial, and friendly—a standard for the royal house.

sentences.zh: 行年八十，被羸老之疾，拘囚環堵之間，顧眄鉤戟之下，呼嗟憤恚，失寢忘食，不知悲翁何以堪此！

translations.literal: At eighty years, afflicted with frail old age, imprisoned within four walls, looking up at halberds above him, sighing in anger and resentment, losing sleep and forgetting food—who knows how an old man in sorrow can bear this!
translations.idiomatic: At eighty, worn by age and illness, imprisoned within four walls, staring up at the halberds of his guards, sighing in rage and resentment, unable to sleep or eat—who can say how much an old man in such sorrow can endure!

sentences.zh: 伏聞希烈之母，鐘念幼子，目不絕泣，求責希烈；

translations.literal: I have heard that Xilie's mother, deeply mindful of her younger son, weeps without cease and demands that Xilie account for himself;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Li Xilie's mother, fixated on her younger son, weeps without cease and calls her son to account;

sentences.zh: 又希烈妻祖母郭及妻妹封並逮捕京師。

translations.literal: Moreover Xilie's wife's grandmother Guo and his wife's younger sister Feng were both arrested and brought to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Xilie's wife's grandmother Guo and his wife's younger sister Feng were both arrested and brought to the capital.

sentences.zh: 此三人留之無益，請寘境上以贖真卿，先降詔書，分明諭告。

translations.literal: To keep these three persons is of no benefit; I ask that they be placed on the border to ransom Zhenqing, and that an edict be issued first with clear instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Keeping these three women serves no purpose; I ask that they be sent to the border country to ransom Yan Zhenqing, and that an edict be issued first with clear instructions.

sentences.zh: 且希烈知真卿人望，不敢加害，既無嫌隙，但因循未遣耳。

translations.literal: Moreover Xilie knows Zhenqing's public standing and dares not harm him; there is no rancor between them, and he has only delayed sending him back through routine.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Xilie knows Yan Zhenqing's standing among men and dares not harm him; there is no feud between them, and he has merely delayed his return through inertia.

sentences.zh: 若歸其親愛，賊亦何吝還一使哉？

translations.literal: If their loved ones are returned, would the rebel begrudge sending back one envoy?
translations.idiomatic: If their kin are returned to him, would the rebel begrudge sending back a single envoy?

sentences.zh: 臣又聞真卿所遣兄子峴及家僮從官奉表來者五輩，皆留中，其子頵等拳拳實希一見，望許休澣，告以安否。

translations.literal: I further hear that the five parties whom Zhenqing sent—his nephew Xian and household servants and attendants bearing memorials—were all kept within the palace; his son Yun and the others earnestly hope for one meeting; I beg permission on a day of rest from audience to tell them whether he is safe.
translations.idiomatic: I further hear that of the five parties Yan Zhenqing sent—his nephew Xian, household servants, and attendants bearing memorials—all were held within the palace; his son Yun and the others earnestly hope for one audience; I beg that on a day of rest from court they be told whether he is safe.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，盧杞持之，不報。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Lu Qi held it and no reply was made.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Lu Qi withheld it and no reply was issued.

sentences.zh: 朱泚反，詭姓名伏匿城中，著《史遁先生傳》。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he used a false name and hid in the city, composing the Biography of Master Shitun.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled, Zhang Jian assumed a false name and hid within the city, writing the Biography of Master Shitun.

sentences.zh: 京師平，擢左拾遺。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, he was promoted to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was pacified, he was promoted to Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 詔復用杞為刺史，薦與陳京、趙需等論杞奸惡傾覆不當用，入對挺確，德宗納之。

translations.literal: An edict proposed reappointing Qi as prefect; Jian, with Chen Jing, Zhao Xu, and others, argued that Qi's wickedness and tendency to overturn affairs made him unfit for use; entering audience he spoke firmly, and Dezong accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict proposed reappointing Lu Qi as prefect; Zhang Jian, with Chen Jing and Zhao Xu, argued that Qi's treachery and habit of overturning affairs made him unfit for office; he spoke firmly in audience, and Emperor Dezong accepted their view.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，帝親郊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan the emperor personally performed the suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenyuan the emperor performed the suburban sacrifice in person.

sentences.zh: 時更兵亂，禮物殘替，用薦為太常博士，參綴典儀，略如舊章。

translations.literal: At that time, after repeated warfare, ritual objects were damaged and missing; Jian was appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to help restore the ceremonies, roughly according to the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: By then repeated warfare had left ritual vessels damaged or lost; Zhang Jian was made an erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to help restore the rites, roughly along the old regulations.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書關播持節送鹹安公主於回紇，以薦為判官。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Guan Bo, bearing credentials to escort Princess Xian'an to the Uyghurs, took Jian as his aide.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Guan Bo, bearing credentials to escort Princess Xian'an to the Uyghurs, took Zhang Jian as his aide.

sentences.zh: 還，遷工部員外郎。

translations.literal: On return he was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢諫議大夫，復為史館修撰。

translations.literal: After a long while he was promoted to Remonstrating Doctor and again served as compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was promoted to remonstrating doctor and again served as a compiler in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 方裴延齡用事，中傷俊良，建白無不當帝意。

translations.literal: Just then Pei Yanling was in power, slandering worthy men; whatever he proposed pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Pei Yanling held power, slandering worthy men; whatever he proposed pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 薦將疏其惡，延齡知之，因言於帝曰：「諫議論朝政得失，史官書人君善惡，二者不可兼。

translations.literal: Jian was about to memorialize his wickedness; Yanling learned of it and therefore said to the emperor: "A remonstrator discusses the gains and losses of court policy, and the historiographer records the ruler's good and evil—one person cannot do both."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian was about to memorialize Yanling's crimes; Yanling learned of it and told the emperor, "A remonstrator debates the rights and wrongs of court policy, and the historiographer records the ruler's good and evil—one man cannot do both."

sentences.zh: 」薦改秘書少監。

translations.literal: " Jian was changed to vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian was transferred to vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 延齡必欲以罪斥廢之。

translations.literal: Yanling was determined to find fault and have him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling was determined to find some charge by which to have him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 會遣使冊回鶻毗伽懷信可汗，使薦至回鶻。

translations.literal: It happened that envoys were sent to invest the Uyghur Qaghan Pijia Huai Xin; Jian was sent to the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that envoys were sent to invest the Uyghur qaghan Pijia Huai Xin, and Zhang Jian was dispatched to the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 還為監。

translations.literal: On return he served as director.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he served as director.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃贊普死，擢薦工部侍郎，為吊祭使。

translations.literal: When the Tibetan tsenpo died, Jian was promoted to vice minister of works and made condolence envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetan emperor died, Zhang Jian was promoted to vice minister of works and made condolence envoy.

sentences.zh: 薦占對詳辯，三使絕域，始兼侍御史、中丞，後大夫。

translations.literal: Jian's responses in audience were detailed and eloquent; on three missions to distant regions he first concurrently held the posts of attendant censor and vice censor-in-chief, then censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian's replies in audience were detailed and eloquent; on three missions beyond the frontier he first concurrently held the posts of attendant censor and vice censor-in-chief, then censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 次赤嶺，被病卒，年六十一，吐蕃傳其柩以歸。

translations.literal: At Chiling he fell ill and died, aged sixty-one; the Tibetans conveyed his coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: At Chiling he fell ill and died, aged sixty-one; the Tibetans escorted his coffin home.

sentences.zh: 順宗立，問至，贈禮部尚書，謚曰憲。

translations.literal: When Shunzong acceded, word arrived; he was posthumously made Minister of Rites, posthumous name Xian.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong acceded, word of his death arrived; he was posthumously made Minister of Rites with the posthumous name Xian.

sentences.zh: 薦自拾遺至侍郎，凡二十年，常兼史館修撰。

translations.literal: From Reminder to vice minister Jian served twenty years, usually also compiling in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: From remonstrator to vice minister, Zhang Jian served twenty years, usually also compiling in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 初，貞元時，京師旱，帝避正殿，減膳，薦白限日以應古制。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Zhenyuan era, when the capital suffered drought, the emperor left the main hall and reduced his meals; Jian proposed limiting the days to accord with ancient regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Zhenyuan era, when the capital suffered drought, the emperor left the main hall and reduced his meals; Zhang Jian proposed limiting the number of days to accord with ancient regulation.

sentences.zh: 及定昭德皇后廟樂，遷獻、懿二祖，定太儀位號、大臣祔廟鼓吹法，莫不參裁，諸儒謂博而詳。

translations.literal: When fixing the temple music for Empress Zhaode, moving the temples of the two ancestors Xian and Yi, and setting the titles of the chief consort, the enshrinement of ministers in the ancestral temple, and the music for the procession—he took part in all, and the classicists called his work broad and detailed.
translations.idiomatic: When the court fixed the temple music for Empress Zhaode, moved the temples of Ancestors Xian and Yi, and set the titles of the chief consort, the rules for enshrining ministers in the ancestral temple, and the music for the procession—he took part in all, and the ritualists called his work broad and detailed.

sentences.zh: 所著書百餘篇。

translations.literal: Works he authored numbered more than a hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: The works he authored numbered more than a hundred pieces.

sentences.zh: 子又新，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Youxin has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhang Youxin has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 孫讀，字聖用，幼穎解。

translations.literal: His grandson Du, style name Shengyong, was clever and quick to understand in youth.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zhang Du, courtesy name Shengyong, was clever and quick to understand from childhood.

sentences.zh: 大中時第進士，鄭薰辟署宣州幕府。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong era he passed the jinshi; Zheng Xun recruited him to the Xuanzhou headquarters staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazhong era he passed the jinshi examination; Zheng Xun recruited him to the staff of the Xuanzhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 中和初為吏部，選牒精允。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhonghe era he headed the Ministry of Personnel; his selection registers were precise and fair.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Zhonghe reign he headed the Ministry of Personnel; his selection registers were precise and fair.

sentences.zh: 調官丐留二年，詔可，榜其事曹門。

translations.literal: He begged to remain in office two years beyond his term; the edict approved, and the matter was posted at the ministry gate.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to remain in office two years beyond his term; the throne approved, and the matter was posted at the ministry gate.

sentences.zh: 後兼弘文館學士，判院事，卒。

translations.literal: Later he also served as academician of the Hongwen Institute, directing its affairs, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he also served as academician of the Hongwen Institute and directed its affairs, then died.

sentences.zh: 趙涓，冀州人。

translations.literal: Zhao Juan, a man of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Juan was a native of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼有文，天寶時第進士，補郾城尉，稍歷臺省。

translations.literal: Gifted in letters from youth, in the Tianbao era he passed the jinshi, was appointed lieutenant of Yancheng, and gradually served in the central ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted in letters from youth, he passed the jinshi in the Tianbao era, was appointed lieutenant of Yancheng, and gradually served in the central ministries.

sentences.zh: 河南王縉引署副元帥府判官。

translations.literal: Wang Jin of Henan recruited him as aide in the deputy marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin of Henan recruited him as aide in the deputy marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 德宗初，為衢州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dezong's reign he was prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Dezong's reign he was prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 始，永泰時，禁中火，近東宮，代宗疑之。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Yongtai era, fire broke out in the palace precinct near the Eastern Palace, and Daizong was suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Yongtai era, fire broke out in the palace precinct near the Eastern Palace, and Emperor Daizong was suspicious.

sentences.zh: 涓以監察御史為巡使，驗治明諦，跡火所來，乃宦人直舍。

translations.literal: Juan, as investigating censor, served as touring commissioner; his examination was clear and exact, and the trail of the fire led to eunuchs' quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Juan, as investigating censor, served as touring commissioner; his investigation was clear and exact, and the trail of the fire led to the eunuchs' quarters.

sentences.zh: 帝在東宮頗德之。

translations.literal: The emperor, then in the Eastern Palace, was much obliged to him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, then heir apparent in the Eastern Palace, was much obliged to him.

sentences.zh: 及治衢，不為觀察使韓滉所容，奏免官。

translations.literal: When he governed Qu, Observation Commissioner Han Huang would not tolerate him and memorialized for his dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: When he governed Quzhou, Observation Commissioner Han Huang would not tolerate him and memorialized for his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 帝見其名，問宰相曰：「是豈永泰時御史乎？

translations.literal: The emperor saw his name and asked the chief minister: "Is this not the censor of the Yongtai era?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw his name and asked the chief minister, "Is this not the censor from the Yongtai era?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「然。

translations.literal: " He answered: "It is."
translations.idiomatic: The minister answered, "It is."

sentences.zh: 」詔拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: " An edict appointed him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 既至，勞之曰：「卿正直，朕所自知，乃以罪聞，不信也。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the emperor comforted him, saying: "You are upright—that I know myself; to hear of you on a charge of crime—I do not believe it."
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, the emperor comforted him, saying, "You are upright—that I know for myself; to hear of you on a charge of crime—I do not believe it."

sentences.zh: 」命典吏部選。

translations.literal: " He was ordered to preside over personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to preside over personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 從狩梁。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor on the hunt at Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor on the campaign at Liang.

sentences.zh: 興元元年卒，贈戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Xingyuan and was posthumously made Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Xingyuan and was posthumously made Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 子博宣，亦擢進士第。

translations.literal: His son Boxuan also passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhao Boxuan also passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 藻翰豪邁，沈於酒，傲忽少檢。

translations.literal: His literary style was bold and unrestrained; he was sunk in wine and arrogant and heedless.
translations.idiomatic: His literary style was bold and unrestrained; he was sunk in wine and arrogant and heedless.

sentences.zh: 陳許曲環辟署於府，久不能堪，乃誣「受吳少誠金為反間，數言休咎惑眾」。

translations.literal: Qu Huan of Chenxu recruited him to his staff; unable to bear it long, Huan falsely charged that "he had received gold from Wu Shaoqing as a spy and repeatedly spoke of omens to mislead the crowd."
translations.idiomatic: Qu Huan of Chenxu recruited him to his staff; unable to bear him long, Huan falsely charged that he had received gold from Wu Shaoqing as a spy and repeatedly spoke of omens to mislead the crowd.

sentences.zh: 有詔杖四十，流康州，時人冤之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered forty strokes of the staff and exile to Kangzhou; people at the time considered it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered forty strokes of the staff and exile to Kangzhou; people at the time considered it unjust.

sentences.zh: 李紓，字仲舒。

translations.literal: Li Shu, style name Zhongshu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shu, whose courtesy name was Zhongshu.

sentences.zh: 始仕為校書郎，大歷初，李季卿薦為左補闕，遷累中書舍人。

translations.literal: He first served as proofreader; in the early Dali era Li Jiqing recommended him as Left Supplementation Officer, and he was promoted in succession to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as proofreader; in the early Dali reign Li Jiqing recommended him as Left Supplementation Officer, and he rose in succession to Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 德宗居奉天，繇禮部侍郎選為同州刺史。

translations.literal: When Dezong was at Fengtian, he was selected from Vice Minister of Rites to be prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong was at Fengtian, Shu was selected from vice minister of rites to be prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝次梁，紓委城趨行在，擢兵部侍郎、高邑伯。

translations.literal: When the emperor halted at Liang, Shu abandoned his prefecture and hurried to the imperial camp, and was promoted to Vice Minister of War and Baron of Gaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor halted at Liang, Li Shu abandoned his prefecture and hurried to the imperial camp, and was promoted to vice minister of war and Baron of Gaoyi.

sentences.zh: 建言享武成王廟不宜與文宣王等，制從之。

translations.literal: He proposed that sacrifices to the Martial Completion King should not be ranked with the Cultured Sagely King; an edict followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that sacrifices to the Martial Completion King should not be ranked with those to the Cultured Sagely King; an edict followed his view.

sentences.zh: 紓性樂易，喜接後進。

translations.literal: Shu was easygoing by nature and delighted in welcoming younger men.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shu was easygoing by nature and delighted in welcoming younger men.

sentences.zh: 其自奉養頗華裕，不為齪齪崖檢。

translations.literal: His own maintenance of himself was quite lavish; he was not finicky or constrained.
translations.idiomatic: His own way of living was quite lavish; he was not finicky or constrained.

sentences.zh: 官雖貴，則遊縱自如。

translations.literal: Though his office was exalted, he roamed and relaxed as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Though his office was exalted, he roamed and relaxed as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 奉詔為《興元紀功述》及它郊廟樂章，論撰甚多。

translations.literal: By imperial command he composed the Account of Achievements at Xingyuan and other suburban and temple hymns; his writings were numerous.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial command he composed the Account of Achievements at Xingyuan and other suburban and temple hymns; his writings were numerous.

sentences.zh: 進吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 年六十二卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-two and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-two and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 鄭雲達，系本滎陽。

translations.literal: Zheng Yunda traced his lineage to Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yunda traced his lineage to Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 父戶，為郾城尉，州刺史移職，民之暴謷者遮道留，戶誅殺六七人。

translations.literal: His father Hu served as lieutenant of Yancheng; when the prefect was transferred, violent complainers blocked the road to detain him, and Hu killed six or seven men.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zheng Hu served as lieutenant of Yancheng; when the prefect was transferred, violent protesters blocked the road to detain him, and Hu killed six or seven men.

sentences.zh: 采訪使奇之，言狀，擢北海尉。

translations.literal: The touring commissioner was impressed, reported the facts, and Hu was promoted to lieutenant of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: The touring commissioner was impressed, reported the facts, and Hu was promoted to lieutenant of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，縣民孫俊驅市人以應，戶率眾擊殺之。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, a county man named Sun Jun drove market people to respond; Hu led the crowd and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, a county man named Sun Jun drove market people to join the rebels; Hu led the crowd and killed him.

sentences.zh: 改登州司馬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military aide of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military aide of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 李光弼表為武寧府判官，遷沂州刺史，諭降賊李浩五千人。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi memorialized him as aide in the Wuning headquarters; he was promoted to prefect of Yizhou and persuaded five thousand of the bandit Li Hao to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi memorialized him as aide in the Wuning headquarters; he was promoted to prefect of Yizhou and persuaded five thousand of the bandit Li Hao to surrender.

sentences.zh: 終滁州刺史。

translations.literal: He ended as prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 雲達為人誕譎敢言，已登進士第，去客燕朔，朱泚善之，表為掌書記，妻以滔女。

translations.literal: Yunda was by nature boastful and bold in speech; having passed the jinshi, he left to sojourn in Yan and the northern frontier; Zhu Ci favored him, memorialized him as chief secretary, and gave him his daughter Taor's hand in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yunda was boastful and bold in speech by nature; having passed the jinshi, he left to sojourn in Yan and the northern frontier; Zhu Ci favored him, appointed him chief secretary, and gave him Zhu Tao's daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 泚將朝，使雲達先入奏，同府蔡廷玉譖於泚，奏貶為平州參軍。

translations.literal: When Ci was about to attend court, he sent Yunda ahead to memorialize; Cai Tingyu of the same office slandered him to Ci, and a memorial demoted Yunda to military aide of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci was about to attend court, he sent Yunda ahead to present a memorial; Cai Tingyu of the same office slandered him to Ci, and a memorial demoted Yunda to military aide of Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 滔代泚將，復辟雲達為判官。

translations.literal: Tao replaced Ci as general and again recruited Yunda as aide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao replaced Ci as general and again recruited Yunda as his aide.

sentences.zh: 廷玉與要藉官朱體微它日與泚從容言：「滔非長者，不可付以兵。

translations.literal: Tingyu and the credential officer Zhu Tiwei one day spoke at ease with Ci: "Tao is not a man of mature judgment and cannot be entrusted with troops."
translations.idiomatic: Cai Tingyu and the credential officer Zhu Tiwei one day spoke at ease with Ci, saying, "Tao is not a man of mature judgment and cannot be entrusted with troops."

sentences.zh: 」雲達數漏其語以怒滔，故滔論廷玉等，皆得罪死。

translations.literal: " Yunda repeatedly leaked their words to anger Tao; therefore Tao prosecuted Tingyu and the others, and all were condemned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yunda repeatedly leaked their words to anger Tao; therefore Tao prosecuted Tingyu and the others, and all were condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 滔助田悅，雲達諫，不從，遂棄室自歸。

translations.literal: Tao aided Tian Yue; Yunda remonstrated but was not followed, so he abandoned his household and returned on his own.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao aided Tian Yue, Yunda remonstrated but was not heeded, so he abandoned his household and returned on his own.

sentences.zh: 德宗悅，擢諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Dezong was pleased and promoted him to Remonstrating Doctor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong was pleased and promoted him to remonstrating doctor.

sentences.zh: 帝在梁，雲達依李晟，晟表以禮部侍郎為軍司馬，時時咨逮戎略。

translations.literal: When the emperor was at Liang, Yunda relied on Li Sheng; Sheng memorialized that he be made army marshal with the title of Vice Minister of Rites, and often consulted him on military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was at Liang, Yunda relied on Li Sheng; Sheng memorialized that he be made army marshal with the title of vice minister of rites, and often consulted him on military strategy.

sentences.zh: 元和初，為京兆尹，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yuanhe reign he was metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao and died.

sentences.zh: 弟方達，悖悍，結徒剽劫，父欲殺之，不克。

translations.literal: His younger brother Fangda was violent and fierce, gathered a band to plunder and rob; the father wished to kill him but could not.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Fangda was violent and fierce and gathered a band to plunder and rob; their father wished to kill him but could not.

sentences.zh: 雲達自劾「不能教，恐赤臣家」。

translations.literal: Yunda impeached himself: "Unable to teach him, I fear I will bring shame on the clan."
translations.idiomatic: Yunda impeached himself, saying, "Unable to teach him, I fear I will bring shame on the clan."

sentences.zh: 詔錮死黔州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him imprisoned and put to death in Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Fangda imprisoned and put to death in Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 徐岱，字處仁，蘇州嘉興人，世農家子。

translations.literal: Xu Dai, style name Churen, was a man of Jiaxing in Suzhou, from a farming family for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Dai, courtesy name Churen, came from Jiaxing in Suzhou, from a family of farmers for generations.

sentences.zh: 於學無所不通，辯論明銳，座人常屈。

translations.literal: In learning there was nothing he did not master; in debate he was sharp and clear, and those seated with him often yielded.
translations.idiomatic: In learning there was nothing he had not mastered; in debate he was sharp and clear, and those seated with him often yielded.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，劉晏表為校書郎。

translations.literal: In the Dali era Liu Yan memorialized him as proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali reign Liu Yan memorialized him as proofreader.

sentences.zh: 觀察使李棲筠欽其賢，署所居為「復禮鄉」。

translations.literal: Observation Commissioner Li Qiyun admired his worth and titled his residence "Restoring Rites Village."
translations.idiomatic: Observation Commissioner Li Qiyun admired his worth and titled his residence Restoring Rites Village.

sentences.zh: 名達於朝，擢偃師尉。

translations.literal: His fame reached the court and he was promoted to lieutenant of Yanshi.
translations.idiomatic: His fame reached the court and he was promoted to lieutenant of Yanshi.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使蔣鎮薦為太常博士，專掌禮事。

translations.literal: Rites Commissioner Jiang Zhen recommended him as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, specializing in ritual affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Rites Commissioner Jiang Zhen recommended him as an erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, specializing in ritual affairs.

sentences.zh: 從德宗出奉天，以膳部員外郎兼博士。

translations.literal: He followed Dezong in leaving Fengtian and served as vice director of the Board of Provisions, concurrently as erudite.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Dezong in leaving Fengtian and served as vice director of the Board of Provisions, concurrently as erudite.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，為太子、諸王侍讀，遷給事中、史館修撰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he was reader for the crown prince and imperial princes, then promoted to Secretariat Receptionist and compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Zhenyuan he was reader for the crown prince and imperial princes, then promoted to secretariat receptionist and compiler in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 帝以誕日歲歲詔佛老者大論麟德殿，並召岱及趙需、許孟容、韋渠牟講說。

translations.literal: On his birthday each year the emperor ordered Buddhist and Daoist elders to debate in the Qinde Hall, and summoned Dai together with Zhao Xu, Xu Mengrong, and Wei Qumou to lecture.
translations.idiomatic: On his birthday each year the emperor ordered Buddhist and Daoist elders to debate in the Qinde Hall, and summoned Dai together with Zhao Xu, Xu Mengrong, and Wei Qumou to lecture.

sentences.zh: 始三家若矛楯然，卒而同歸於善。

translations.literal: At first the three schools were like spear and shield, but in the end all returned to the good.
translations.idiomatic: At first the three schools clashed like spear against shield, but in the end all returned to the good.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賚予有差。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed rewards in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed rewards in varying measure.

sentences.zh: 兩宮恩遇無比。

translations.literal: The two palaces favored him beyond compare.
translations.idiomatic: The two palaces favored him beyond compare.

sentences.zh: 性篤慎，至宮殿中語未嘗近之，不談人短，宗族孤孺者皆為婚嫁。

translations.literal: By nature he was sincere and cautious; in the palace he never approached improper speech, did not discuss others' faults, and arranged marriages for orphaned and young kin.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was sincere and cautious; in the palace he never approached improper speech, did not discuss others' faults, and arranged marriages for orphaned and young kin.

sentences.zh: 然吝嗇，自持家管鑰，世所譏雲。

translations.literal: Yet he was stingy, keeping the household keys himself—a thing the age mocked.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was stingy, keeping the household keys himself—a thing his contemporaries mocked.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 王仲舒，字弘中，并州祁人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongshu, style name Hongzhong, was a man of Qi in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongshu, courtesy name Hongzhong, came from Qi in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少客江南，與梁肅、楊憑遊，有文稱。

translations.literal: In youth he sojourned in the south, associated with Liang Su and Yang Ping, and had a literary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he sojourned in the south, associated with Liang Su and Yang Ping, and had a literary reputation.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，賢良方正高第，拜左拾遺。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era he took high rank in the Exemplary and Upright examination and was appointed Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyuan era he took high rank in the Exemplary and Upright examination and was appointed Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 德宗欲相裴延齡，與陽城交章言不可。

translations.literal: Dezong wished to make Pei Yanling chief minister; he and Yang Cheng submitted successive memorials saying it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong wished to make Pei Yanling chief minister; he and Yang Cheng submitted successive memorials saying it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 後入閣，帝顧宰相指曰：「是豈王仲舒邪？

translations.literal: Later entering the privy council, the emperor looked at the chief minister and pointed, saying: "Is that not Wang Zhongshu?"
translations.idiomatic: Later, entering the privy council, the emperor looked at the chief minister and pointed, saying, "Is that not Wang Zhongshu?"

sentences.zh: 」俄改右補闕，遷禮部考功員外郎。

translations.literal: " Soon he was changed to Right Supplementation Officer and promoted to Vice Director of Examination in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was changed to Right Supplementation Officer and promoted to vice director of examination in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 奏議詳雅，省中伏其能。

translations.literal: His memorials and proposals were detailed and elegant; within the ministry all submitted to his ability.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials and proposals were detailed and elegant; within the ministry all submitted to his ability.

sentences.zh: 坐累為連州司戶參軍，再徙荊南節度參謀。

translations.literal: Through implication in a case he was made military aide of Lianzhou, then twice transferred as staff officer on the Jingnan frontier command.
translations.idiomatic: Through implication in a case he was made military aide of Lianzhou, then twice transferred as staff officer on the Jingnan frontier command.

sentences.zh: 元和初，召為吏部員外郎，未幾，知制誥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was summoned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel; before long he drafted edicts.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yuanhe reign he was summoned as vice director of the Ministry of Personnel; before long he drafted edicts.

sentences.zh: 楊憑得罪斥去，無敢過其家，仲舒屢存之。

translations.literal: When Yang Ping was condemned and driven out, none dared visit his house; Zhongshu repeatedly called on him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Ping was condemned and driven out, none dared visit his house; Zhongshu repeatedly called on him.

sentences.zh: 將直憑冤，貶峽州刺史，母喪解。

translations.literal: About to speak straight for Ping's injustice, he was demoted to prefect of Xiazhou; when his mother died he left office.
translations.idiomatic: About to speak straight for Ping's injustice, he was demoted to prefect of Xiazhou; when his mother died he left office.

sentences.zh: 服除，為婺州刺史。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 州疫旱，人徙死幾空；

translations.literal: The prefecture suffered plague and drought; people fled and died until the district was nearly empty;
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture suffered plague and drought; people fled and died until the district was nearly empty;

sentences.zh: 居五年，裏閭增完，就加金紫服。

translations.literal: after five years in office the lanes and hamlets were restored and he was given the gold-and-purple robe on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: after five years in office the lanes and hamlets were restored and he was given the gold-and-purple robe on the spot.

sentences.zh: 徙蘇州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 堤松江為路，變屋瓦，絕火災，賦調嘗與民為期，不擾自辦。

translations.literal: He diked the Song River as a road, changed roof tiles, cut off fire disasters, and when levying taxes always set terms with the people so that without disturbance they met them themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He diked the Song River as a road, changed roof tiles to cut off fire disasters, and when levying taxes always set terms with the people so that without disturbance they met them themselves.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，每言仲舒之文可思，最宜為誥，有古風。

translations.literal: When Muzong acceded, he often said Zhongshu's writings were worth pondering, most fit for edicts, with an antique style.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong acceded, he often said Zhongshu's writings were worth pondering, most fit for edicts, with an antique style.

sentences.zh: 召為中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 既至，視同列率新進少年，居不樂，曰：「豈可復治筆研於其間哉！

translations.literal: When he arrived, seeing his colleagues mostly newly advanced youths, he was discontent and said: "How can I again grind ink among them!
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, seeing his colleagues mostly newly advanced youths, he was discontent and said, "How can I again grind ink among them!

sentences.zh: 吾久棄外，周知俗病利，得治之，不自愧。

translations.literal: I have long been cast outside and know well the ills and profits of custom; if I can govern, I will not be ashamed."
translations.idiomatic: I have long been cast outside and know well the ills and profits of custom; if I can govern, I will not be ashamed."

sentences.zh: 」宰相聞之，除江西觀察使。

translations.literal: " When the chief minister heard this, he was made Jiangxi observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief minister heard this, he was made Jiangxi observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 初，江西榷酒利多佗州十八，民私釀，歲抵死不絕，谷數斛易鬥酒。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jiangxi's monopoly wine profits exceeded those of other prefectures by eighteenfold; the people brewed in secret, and each year some were condemned to death without cease—a few hu of grain traded for a dou of wine.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jiangxi's monopoly wine profits exceeded those of other prefectures by eighteenfold; the people brewed in secret, and each year some were condemned to death without cease—a few hu of grain traded for a dou of wine.

sentences.zh: 仲舒罷酤錢九十萬。

translations.literal: Zhongshu abolished nine hundred thousand in monopoly revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu abolished nine hundred thousand in monopoly revenue.

sentences.zh: 吏坐失官息錢五十萬，悉產不能償，仲舒焚簿書，脫械不問。

translations.literal: Officials were charged with losing fifty thousand in official interest money; their entire property could not repay; Zhongshu burned the account books and released them from shackles without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were charged with losing fifty thousand in official interest money; their entire property could not repay; Zhongshu burned the account books and released them from shackles without inquiry.

sentences.zh: 水旱，民賦不入，嘆曰：「我當減燕樂他用可乎！

translations.literal: In flood and drought the people's taxes did not come in; he sighed: "Shall I reduce banquets and music and use it elsewhere!
translations.idiomatic: In flood and drought the people's taxes did not come in; he sighed, "Shall I reduce banquets and music and use the savings elsewhere!

sentences.zh: 」為出錢二千萬代之。

translations.literal: " He paid out twenty million to cover it.
translations.idiomatic: He paid out twenty million to cover it.

sentences.zh: 有為佛老法、興浮屠祠屋者，皆驅出境。

translations.literal: Those who practiced Buddhist or Daoist law or raised Buddhist temple buildings were all driven beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: Those who practiced Buddhist or Daoist law or raised Buddhist temple buildings were all driven beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，年六十二，贈左散騎常侍，謚曰成。

translations.literal: He died in office, aged sixty-two, posthumously made Left Regular Cavalry Attendant, posthumous name Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office, aged sixty-two, posthumously made Left Regular Cavalry Attendant with the posthumous name Cheng.

sentences.zh: 仲舒尚義概，所居急民廢置，自為科條，初若煩密，久皆稱其便。

translations.literal: Zhongshu valued righteousness and breadth of spirit; wherever he served he urgently attended to what the people had abandoned or needed, setting regulations himself; at first they seemed troublesome and detailed, but in time all praised their convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu valued righteousness and breadth of spirit; wherever he served he urgently attended to what the people had abandoned or needed, setting regulations himself; at first they seemed troublesome and detailed, but in time all praised their convenience.

sentences.zh: 馮伉，魏州元城人，徙貫京兆。

translations.literal: Feng Kang, a man of Yuancheng in Weizhou, later registered residence in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Kang came from Yuancheng in Weizhou and later registered residence in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 第五經、宏辭，調長安尉。

translations.literal: He passed the fifth classics and the Hongci examinations and was appointed lieutenant of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the fifth classics and the Hongci examinations and was appointed lieutenant of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 三遷膳部員外郎，為睦王等侍讀。

translations.literal: Three promotions to vice director of the Board of Provisions; he was reader for Prince of Mu and others.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he was vice director of the Board of Provisions and reader for the Prince of Mu and others.

sentences.zh: 李抱真卒，伉持節臨吊，歸之帛，不受，又致京師，伉上表固拒。

translations.literal: When Li Baozhen died, Kang bore credentials to condole; returning, Baozhen's silk was not accepted; when it was again sent to the capital, Kang submitted a memorial firmly refusing.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Baozhen died, Kang bore credentials to offer condolences; on his return Baozhen's gift of silk was not accepted; when it was again sent to the capital, Kang submitted a memorial firmly refusing.

sentences.zh: 於是醴泉令缺，宰相高選，德宗曰：「前使澤潞不受幣者，其人清，可用也。

translations.literal: Then the magistracy of Liquan was vacant; the chief minister made a high selection; Dezong said: "The man who earlier went to Zelu and did not accept gifts—that man is pure and can be used."
translations.idiomatic: Then the magistracy of Liquan was vacant; the chief minister made a high selection; Emperor Dezong said, "The man who earlier went to Zelu and did not accept gifts—that man is pure and can be used."

sentences.zh: 」遂以授伉。

translations.literal: " He was then given to Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was then given the post.

sentences.zh: 縣多嚚猾，數犯法，伉為著《諭蒙書》十四篇，大抵勸之務農、進學而教以忠孝。

translations.literal: The county had many violent and crafty men who repeatedly broke the law; Kang composed for them the Exhortation to the Untaught in fourteen chapters, mostly urging them to devote themselves to farming and advance in learning while teaching loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: The county had many violent and crafty men who repeatedly broke the law; Kang composed for them the Exhortation to the Untaught in fourteen chapters, mostly urging them to devote themselves to farming and advance in learning while teaching loyalty and filial piety.

sentences.zh: 鄉鄉授之，使轉相教督。

translations.literal: Village by village it was handed out, so that they might teach and supervise one another.
translations.idiomatic: Village by village it was handed out, so that they might teach and supervise one another.

sentences.zh: 居七年，韋渠牟薦為給事中、皇太子諸王侍讀。

translations.literal: After seven years Wei Qumou recommended him as Secretariat Receptionist and reader for the crown prince and imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years Wei Qumou recommended him as secretariat receptionist and reader for the crown prince and imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 對殿中，賜金紫服。

translations.literal: In audience in the hall he was granted the gold-and-purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: In audience in the hall he was granted the gold-and-purple robe.

sentences.zh: 進兵部侍郎，出為同州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of War and went out as prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of war and went out as prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 以散騎常侍召，領國子祭酒者再。

translations.literal: Summoned as Regular Attendant, he twice headed the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as regular attendant, he twice headed the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十六，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-six, posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died, aged sixty-six, posthumously made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 庾敬休，字順之，鄧州新野人。

translations.literal: Yu Jingxiu, style name Shunzhi, was a man of Xinye in Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jingxiu, courtesy name Shunzhi, came from Xinye in Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖光烈，與弟光先不受安祿山偽官，遁去。

translations.literal: His grandfather Guanglie and his younger brother Guangxian did not accept An Lushan's false offices and fled.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu Guanglie and his younger brother Guangxian did not accept An Lushan's false offices and fled.

sentences.zh: 光烈終大理少卿，光先吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Guanglie ended as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review; Guangxian as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Guanglie ended as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review; Guangxian as vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 父何，當朱泚反，又與弟倬逃山谷，不臣賊。

translations.literal: His father He, when Zhu Ci rebelled, again fled with his younger brother Zhuo into the mountains and valleys and did not serve the rebel.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu He, when Zhu Ci rebelled, again fled with his younger brother Zhuo into the mountains and valleys and did not serve the rebel.

sentences.zh: 官兵部郎中。

translations.literal: He ended as director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 敬休擢進士第，又中宏辭，辟宣州幕府。

translations.literal: Jingxiu passed the jinshi and also passed the Hongci; he was recruited to the Xuanzhou headquarters staff.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxiu passed the jinshi and also passed the Hongci examination; he was recruited to the Xuanzhou headquarters staff.

sentences.zh: 入拜右補闕、起居舍人，建言：「天子視朝，宰相群臣以次對，言可傳後者，承旨宰相示左右起居，則載錄，季送史官，如故事。

translations.literal: Entering court he was appointed Right Supplementation Officer and Attendant on the Imperial Diary, and proposed: "When the Son of Heaven holds audience, the chief minister and officials speak in turn; words fit to be handed down, the chief minister by edict shows to the Left and Right Attendants on the Imperial Diary, and they are recorded and quarterly sent to the historiographers, as in the old precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Entering court he was appointed Right Supplementation Officer and attendant on the imperial diary, and proposed that when the Son of Heaven held audience, the chief minister and officials should speak in turn, and words fit to be handed down should be shown by the chief minister by edict to the left and right attendants on the imperial diary to be recorded and sent quarterly to the historiographers, as in the old precedent.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved.

sentences.zh: 既而執政以幾密有不可露，罷之。

translations.literal: Soon the administration, on grounds that some matters were secret and could not be disclosed, abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the administration, on grounds that some matters were secret and could not be disclosed, abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 文宗將立魯王為太子，慎選師傅，敬休以戶部侍郎兼魯王傅。

translations.literal: When Wenzong was about to establish the Prince of Lu as heir, tutors were carefully chosen; Jingxiu was made tutor to the Prince of Lu while also Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong was about to establish the Prince of Lu as heir, tutors were carefully chosen; Jingxiu was made tutor to the Prince of Lu while also vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 初，劍南西川、山南道歲征茶，戶部自遣巡院主之，募賈人入錢京師。

translations.literal: Earlier, southwestern Sichuan and the Shannan circuit levied tea each year; the Ministry of Revenue itself sent touring offices to supervise, recruiting merchants to pay money into the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, southwestern Sichuan and the Shannan circuit levied tea each year; the Ministry of Revenue itself sent touring offices to supervise, recruiting merchants to pay money into the capital.

sentences.zh: 太和初，崔元略奏責本道主當歲以四萬緡上度支。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, Cui Yuanlue memorialized that the circuit responsible each year should deliver forty thousand strings to the Department of Public Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taihe reign, Cui Yuanlue memorialized that the circuit responsible each year should deliver forty thousand strings to the Department of Public Revenue.

sentences.zh: 久之，逗留多不至。

translations.literal: After a long while many delayed and did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while many delayed and did not arrive.

sentences.zh: 敬休始請置院秭歸，收度支錢，乃無逋沒。

translations.literal: Jingxiu first proposed establishing an office at Zigui to collect the Department's money, and then there were no shortfalls.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxiu first proposed establishing an office at Zigui to collect the department's money, and then there were no shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 又言：「蜀道米價騰踴，百姓流亡，請以本道闕官職田賑貧民。

translations.literal: He also said: "On the Sichuan road grain prices soar; the common people flee; I ask that vacant official fields in this circuit be used to relieve the poor."
translations.idiomatic: He also said that on the Sichuan road grain prices soared, the common people fled, and he asked that vacant official fields in the circuit be used to relieve the poor.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved.

sentences.zh: 再為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Again he was Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Again he was Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 敬休夷淡，多容可，不飲酒食肉，不邇聲色。

translations.literal: Jingxiu was mild and plain, much tolerant and agreeable, did not drink wine or eat meat, and did not approach music and beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxiu was mild and plain, much tolerant and agreeable, did not drink wine or eat meat, and did not approach music and beauty.

sentences.zh: 弟簡休，亦至工部侍郎。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jianxiu also reached Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jianxiu also reached vice minister of works.
